name: Generating Assessments
title: Generating Assessments
answer: Generating assessments means using AI to produce quiz questions, exam items, rubrics, discussion prompts and practice problems from course materials such as lecture notes, readings or a syllabus. It covers the whole item lifecycle, from drafting stems and distractors to aligning each question with a stated learning outcome. The work sits with instructors and instructional designers rather than with machine learning engineers, and it is judged by whether the resulting items measure what the course claims to teach.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Generating assessments means using AI to produce quiz questions, exam items, rubrics, discussion prompts and practice problems from course materials such as lecture notes, readings or a syllabus. It covers the whole item lifecycle, from drafting stems and distractors to aligning each question with a stated learning outcome. The work sits with instructors and instructional designers rather than with machine learning engineers, and it is judged by whether the resulting items measure what the course claims to teach.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Most of this work happens in general purpose chat assistants and in features built into learning management systems and assessment platforms. A typical setup feeds the model a passage, a set of learning objectives and a requested format, then returns items in plain text or a structured file that can be imported into a quiz bank. Some institutions run models locally or through a contracted service so that unpublished exam content does not leave their network.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The usual pattern is to supply source material and constraints, then ask for items at a specified difficulty and cognitive level, often with the correct answer and a short rationale. Instructors review every generated item, because models readily produce plausible but wrong answers, ambiguous stems and distractors that are also defensible. Good practice includes testing items on a small group, checking readability, and revising or discarding anything that does not map cleanly to an outcome.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and provenance matter because course readings, textbook passages and past exams may be copyrighted or confidential, and uploading them to a third party service can breach policy or licence terms. Institutions increasingly require disclosure of AI assistance in assessment design and keep records of which model and prompt produced an item. Student data should not be fed into these tools, and generated items should be treated as drafts with a named human owner.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect tighter integration between assessment generators and learning management systems, so items arrive already tagged to outcomes and difficulty. Interest is growing in using response data to flag items that behave poorly and in generating variants for practice and retesting. The open questions are how to keep item banks trustworthy as generation gets cheaper, and how to document provenance well enough that a reviewer can tell where a question came from.
